html:
A university of science and engineering in Haifa, founded in 1912 when the town was part of the Ottoman Empire. It is the oldest university in Israel.

It was founded by Jewish groups, led by a German Jewish aid society, and was meant to train engineers for the Jewish community growing in Palestine under Zionism. In 1913 a fight broke out over whether it should teach in German. Teachers and students struck, and Hebrew won. The outbreak of World War I then delayed the opening, and teaching began only in 1924. Albert Einstein visited in 1923 and helped raise money for it.

Its graduates designed much of Israel's roads, water systems, army technology and later its high tech industry, which grew strongly from the 1990s. Technion researchers have won Nobel prizes in chemistry, among them for the discovery of quasicrystals in 2011. It also runs a campus in New York with Cornell University.
sum: A university of science and engineering in Haifa, founded in 1912 when the town was part of the Ottoman Empire. It is the oldest university in Israel.
